about: MAY this happen at this level — a DIFFERENT question from does-this-collide,
and the one a caller actually asks on the hot path.
It got its own file because it was the divergence nobody could see: the
TypeScript packer grew `accepts` and `maskOf` and the Rust one did not, and
no vector covered the surface, so the suite that exists to keep the two
honest had nothing to say about it.
The trap is the last case. An opinion of `nothing above the bottom` collides
with nobody and permits nothing, so a caller checking only for collisions

coverage.criterion: every state, on a chain and on the two-element powerset, asked at the bottom, the top and a middle
coverage.why: two carriers, not all carriers; the exhaustive cross-check against walking the order lives in the unit tests

cases.name: nothing above the bottom does not collide and permits nothing
